record.original_question: Let Sigma be the set of all triples S of points in the Euclidean plane for which there exist geodesic multinets with exactly three unbalanced vertices located at S and with arbitrarily many balanced vertices. Is Sigma a measure-zero subset of (R^2)^3?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1.3. Let Σ be the set of all triples S of points of the Euclidean plane such that there exist geodesic multinets with 3 unbalanced vertices at S and arbitrarily many balanced vertices. Is it true that Σ is a set of measure zero (in (R2)3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic multinet is a finite multigraph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose edges are straight line segments (geodesics), where multiple edges between the same pair of vertices are allowed. A vertex $v$ of a geodesic multinet is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ along all edges incident to $v$ (each multi-edge contributing its own unit tangent vector) equals the zero vector; otherwise $v$ is called unbalanced.

Let $\Sigma \subset (\mathbb{R}^2)^3$ be the set of all ordered triples $S = (p_1, p_2, p_3)$ of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ for which, for every positive integer $N$, there exists a geodesic multinet whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the three points of $S$ and which contains at least $N$ balanced vertices.

Determine whether $\Sigma$ has Lebesgue measure zero in $(\mathbb{R}^2)^3 \cong \mathbb{R}^6$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on geodesic nets with three boundary vertices (e.g., Parsch's result that a geodesic net with three boundary vertices on a non-positively curved plane has at most one balanced vertex) and subsequent research up to 2025 on constructing geodesic nets with few boundary vertices and many balanced vertices do not appear to resolve the measure-theoretic question for multinets in the Euclidean plane. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that a geodesic net with three boundary vertices on a non-positively curved plane has at most one balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Related result for nets (not multinets) but does not address the measure-zero question for the multinet setting.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on constructions of geodesic nets with few boundary vertices and many balanced vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the topic is still actively researched without a resolution of the three-vertex multinet measure-zero question.
